run_form.window_unavailable: The computer that would run this has no graphical desktop (for example a Linux server without DISPLAY), so only headless mode is available.
run_form.base_url_hint: Overrides the baseUrl in the scenario file. Leave empty to use the scenario file.

roles.description: Register how each test account logs in and how to tell it is logged in; scenarios use it with login: {{ role: … }}. Each role keeps its own login state, never shared.
roles.notice: Before a run, the role's login is checked; if it is not logged in the run stops at "Login required" without running any step. "Log in" opens a browser window on the computer running the Portal so you can log in yourself (SSO, captchas and two-factor all work); the login state is stored only in this computer's data folder, readable only by you.
roles.no_display: The computer running the Portal has no display, so a browser window for manual login cannot be opened; you can give the role automatic login steps instead.
roles.empty: No login roles yet. Add a role here when a scenario needs to log in.
roles.session_waiting: A browser window is open on the computer running the Portal: log in there, then press "Finish login" or simply close the window.
roles.login_title: Open a browser window on the Portal's computer and log in yourself
roles.check_title: Check in a headless browser whether the login is still valid (logs in automatically when automatic login steps exist)
roles.form_notice: For example: id erp-clerk, name "ERP clerk". The id goes into a scenario's login.role and cannot be changed later.
roles.form_description: Description (optional, e.g. which test account; never a password)
roles.form_check_url_placeholder: A page only visible when logged in; empty means the login URL

roles.form_auto: Automatic login steps (optional, a list of DSL steps)

secrets.form_notice: The value is stored in secrets.json in the data folder, readable only by you; it is never shown again.
needs.title: Before running
recording.description: Record on this computer or paste a codegen recording → DSL draft → step debugging → validation → publish by hand. Recordings are never published directly.
recording.active: Recording {scene}: the browser window and Playwright Inspector are open on the computer running the Portal; close the browser window when you are done.
recording.in_progress: Recording: use the browser on the computer running the Portal and close its window when you are done; the draft appears here automatically.
recording.record_hint: After "Start recording", a browser and the Playwright Inspector open on the computer running the Portal; work as usual and close the browser window when done. Typed values become inputs and password fields become secrets.

recording.mode_replace_hint: Record again from the start URL and replace the whole scenario with the recording (name and category are kept, older revisions stay).

recording.url_continue: Recording continues from the screen where the existing steps end, so no start URL is needed.

target.hint: Headed browser windows appear on the computer that runs the job. On a remote worker, 127.0.0.1 means that worker itself (it starts its own test site too).
workers.description: Register the computers that run scenarios (RPA Worker): paste an invitation to pair, then runs go to them and this computer is no longer taken over by headed browser windows.
workers.notice: Devices connect to this computer's external port. A worker claims jobs and sends the report, screenshots and trace back, so run reports look the same as local ones; a recorder opens the browser for recording, step-by-step debugging and manual logins on that computer. Adding a device creates an invitation (single use, valid for 24 hours); paste it into the app on that computer to pair. Inviting again ends the old pairing immediately. A worker that does not report for over a minute is considered lost: its run is marked failed and is not retried automatically (it may already have had side effects).
workers.api_on: The external port is open at {url} (only the Worker API and pairing; a token or invitation is required).
workers.api_off: The external port is not open, so devices cannot connect and no invitation can be created: stop the portal and start it again with rpa serve --worker-port 8081. The portal pages stay local-only.
workers.local_off: This computer does not run jobs (--no-local-worker); every job goes to remote workers.
workers.empty: No devices yet. Choose "Add device" to create an invitation, then paste it into RPA Worker on that computer.
workers.version_differs: Differs from the portal's code: updating both to the same version is safer.

target.local_url_warning_via_recorder: This scenario's URL points to the local computer (127.0.0.1, localhost). On the server that means the server, and on a remote worker the worker itself, neither of which is the computer you are using. To run it elsewhere, change the URL to the site's LAN address.
workers.form_kind_hint: A worker runs scenarios; a recorder opens the browser for recording, step-by-step debugging and manual logins on that computer (for example your Mac).
recorders.list: RPA Recorder (recording, step-by-step debugging, manual login)
recorders.hint: When you work through a recorder the browser opens on it; scenarios still run on the server or a worker
recorders.active: {count} recording, debugging or manual login sessions in progress
recorders.empty: No recorders yet. Choose Add device and pick RPA Recorder.
recorders.invite_app: On the computer you record on, open RPA Recorder and paste this invitation (it has been copied to the clipboard); with a development setup you can also use the command below.
error.recorder_unauthorized: The recorder's token is wrong or the recorder is disabled. Invite it again from the Devices page of the management portal
error.recorder_offline: Recorder “{name}” is not connected. Make sure RPA Recorder is open
error.recorder_no_display: Recorder “{name}” has no graphical desktop, so it cannot open a browser window
error.recorder_browser_missing: Recorder “{name}” has not downloaded {engine} yet. Download it in RPA Recorder and try again
error.recorder_lost: Lost contact with recorder {name} (no response for over 30 seconds), so this session has ended
error.recorder_restarted: Recorder {name} restarted, so this session has ended
error.recorder_disabled: Recorder {name} was disabled, so this session has ended
error.recorder_removed: Recorder {name} was deleted, so this session has ended
error.recorder_reinvited: Recorder {name} was invited again (the old pairing no longer works), so this session has ended
error.recorder_server_stopped: The management portal stopped, so the session on recorder {name} has ended
error.recorder_hello_first: The recorder must come online first
error.process_not_found: Child process {id} not found (it may have ended)
error.files_invalid: The returned files are not allowed: {detail}
